text: **Hint 1:** Recall that in logistic regression, the probability \( $$p$$ \) is the model's predicted probability that a given datapoint belongs to class $$1$$. The loss function \(\mathcal{L}(\theta)\) is designed to penalize incorrect predictions.\n\n**Hint 2:** Consider the role of the term \( y\log(p) \) in the loss function. What happens to this term when the true class label \( $$y$$ \) is 0? How does this affect the overall loss calculation?
